references.text: The expression 'to take a census' or 'count the heads' is used both here and in Numbers 1, where Moses was commanded to count the men of Israel who were fit for war.
Another census of able-bodied men in Israel, showing the same practice of counting the fighting force.
The principle of counting the people of Israel and the miracle that none were missing is linked to God's protection of His people.
Saul mustered the people in a similar way, and counting the soldiers was a common practice before and after war.
David commanded that the people be counted, showing that a census of fighting men was an established practice in Israel.
Jesus said that He did not lose any of those the Father gave Him, reflecting the idea that none were lost—just as no Israelite soldier was missing.
